# Marketing Sales Analysis and Linear Regression Modeling
This project analyzes marketing expenditure across multiple promotional channels and evaluates the relationship between advertising investment and sales performance using exploratory data analysis and linear regression.

### Distribution Analysis of Numerical Variables
```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

plt.figure(figsize=(12,10))
for i, column in enumerate(numerical_features):
    plt.subplot(3,1,i+1)
    sns.histplot(data[column], color="lightblue", kde=True)
    plt.title(f"Distribution 0f {column}")
    plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
### Outlier Detection Using Boxplots
```{python}
plt.figure(figsize=(10,10))

for i, column in enumerate(numerical_features):
    plt.subplot(3,1,i+1)
    sns.boxplot(x=column, data=data, color="lightgreen")
    plt.title(f"Boxplot of {column}")
    plt.grid(True)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
### Relationship Analysis Between Variables
```{python}
sns.pairplot(data)
plt.show()
```
### Observaations
- A positive relationship is observed between Radio promotion budget and Sales
- A moderate association appears between Social Media and Radio spending
- Sales show stronger linear alignment with Radio expenditure

## 5. Linear Regression Modeling
### Regression Visualization
```{python}
sns.regplot(x="Radio", y="Sales", data=data, scatter_kws={"color":"lightblue"}, line_kws={"color":"red"})
plt.show()
```
### Model Summary and Statistical Interpretation
```{python}
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols
model=ols("Sales ~ Radio", data)
model=model.fit()
print(model.summary())
```
### Residual Distribution Assessment
```{python}
sns.histplot(model.resid, kde=True)
plt.show()
```
### Normality Assessment Using Q–Q Plot
```{python}
import statsmodels.api as sm
sm.qqplot(model.resid, line="s")
plt.show()
```
### Residuals vs Fitted Values Analysis
```{python}
sns.scatterplot(x=model.fittedvalues, y= model.resid)
plt.axhline()
plt.show()
```
## 7. Conclusion

This project explored the relationship between marketing expenditure and sales performance using exploratory data analysis and simple linear regression.

After cleaning the dataset and analyzing variable relationships, **Radio promotion budget** was selected as the predictor variable for modeling sales.

The regression model achieved an **R² score of 0.757**, indicating that approximately **75.7% of the variation in sales can be explained by radio promotion spending**.

The fitted regression equation was:

\[
Sales = 8.17(Radio) + 41.53
\]

Model interpretation suggests that **for every additional one million invested in radio promotion, predicted sales increase by approximately 8.17 million on average**.

Diagnostic evaluation using residual distribution, Q–Q plots, and residual vs fitted analysis indicated that the regression assumptions were reasonably satisfied.

Overall, the analysis demonstrates that **radio advertising expenditure shows a strong positive relationship with sales and can serve as an effective predictor of sales performance within this dataset.**
